instantiated_cells.justification: Section 305.003(a)(2) requires registration of a person who receives compensation or reimbursement of "more than an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter" to communicate directly with members of the legislative or executive branch.
Section 305.003(a)(1) requires registration of a person who "makes a total expenditure of an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter" on lobbying activities.

Section 305.003(b-3) exempts from registration a person who "spends not more than 26 hours, or another amount of time determined by the commission" during a calendar quarter engaging in compensated direct-communication lobbying activity, establishing a 26-hour-per-quarter time standard.

Section 305.0061(c) requires detailed itemized reporting of gifts, awards, or mementos only when the value "exceeds $50 per gift, award, or memento," establishing a $50 per-item itemization threshold below which detailed disclosure is not required (aggregate-only reporting under §305.006(b) applies).

Section 305.003(a) only requires registration (and therefore reporting under §305.006) when expenditures or compensation exceed the statutory floor of $200 per calendar quarter; persons below this threshold are exempt from filing disclosure entirely.

Section 305.003(b-3) sets the time-based exemption in absolute hours (26 hours per calendar quarter), not as a percentage of the individual's compensated time; no statute in Chapter 305 expresses a percent-of-time threshold for filing exemption.

content.text:
I'll analyze each cell based on the Texas statute text provided.

**Row 001**: §305.003(a)(2) sets a compensation threshold of "more than an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter."

**Row 002**: §305.003(a)(1) sets an expenditure threshold of "an amount determined by commission rule but not less than $200 in a calendar quarter."

**Row 003**: §305.003(b-3) provides a time-based exemption: "not more than 26 hours...during the calendar quarter."

**Row 004**: §305.0061 has detail-reporting thresholds (60% of legislative per diem, $50 for gifts), but these are thresholds above which MORE detail is required, not itemization de minimis thresholds. However, $50 is the gift itemization threshold under §305.0061(c).

**Row 005**: §305.003 sets the registration threshold ($200/quarter), which effectively functions as a filing-exemption threshold since no registration = no reports.

**Row 006**: The 26-hour quarterly threshold in §305.003(b-3) is a time-based exemption, but it's expressed in hours, not as a percentage of compensated time. No percentage-based threshold exists.
